# Answer

## Where this happens
At about 7:17–7:23 (437–443 s) the camera pans along the curved wall of trading monitors (Windows XP wallpaper), then jumps to the blonde woman (Kristi, CFO of thinkorswim) talking on a blue desk-phone handset at her cluttered desk in front of the whiteboard wall.

- **Side view** (~439.3–440.3 s): a low three-quarter view of her from her right side, shot past the back of a monitor; the handset is pressed to the right side of her face. A quarter-second extreme close-up of the handset/hair/fingers is hard-cut into the middle of this shot (~439.5–439.75 s).
- **Closer shot** (~440.4–443.4 s): a cut to a tighter shot of her face, still from her right, handset again against her right ear.

## What she must have done
Between the side view and the closer shot she must have **switched the handset from one hand to the other — passed it from her left hand to her right hand.** The two shots are cut together as if continuous, but the phone is not being held by the same hand in both, so a hand change had to happen off-screen (the closer shot was clearly filmed separately and joined by the edit).

## The visible change that shows it
1. **In the side view the hand gripping the handset wears a silver bracelet wristwatch (just above the blazer cuff) and a ring on the ring finger.** That is her left hand: later in the film (~532 s, same black blazer and blue lanyard, same desk) she gestures with both hands and the watch is on her left wrist; the extreme close-up at ~449 s also shows the ring on her left hand. In the side view her left arm reaches up across in front of her body to hold the phone to her right ear, while her other hand is down on the desk holding a pen (bottom right of the frame).
2. **In the closer shot the hand holding the handset is bare — no watch on the wrist and no ring on any finger.** It is her right hand: the arm comes up from her right side, the fingers curl over the front edge of the handset toward her face with the index finger extended along the handset, in a normal same-side grip.

So the wristwatch and ring that were on the phone hand in the side view simply disappear in the closer shot; a bare right hand is now holding the phone. That vanishing watch/ring (plus the reversed grip and arm position) is the visible change, and it can only be explained by the handset having changed hands.

## Note on the ear
The handset stays against the **right** side of her face in both shots (in the side view its top is at her eye level between her hair and her nose, over her right cheek, with the cord dropping from the bottom of the handset toward the phone base on the desk to her right). At a glance the side view can read as if the phone were on the far (left) side of her head, because the visible hand is her left one, but it is the **hand**, not the ear, that changes between the two shots.

criteria.justification: The candidate explicitly states she "passed it from her left hand to her right hand" between the two shots.

Between those two shots she must have lifted, turned and re-seated the

What shows this, explicitly:

- In the side view the receiver hand holds only the receiver. No pen is

- In the closer frontal shot the same hand is seen from the back gripping
  both receiver and pen together. A black pen with a silver conical tip is
  clearly wedged against the receiver, its tip protruding up between the

  down along the receiver. The fat blue mouthpiece with its blue coiled cord

  the cord dropping vertically from the mouthpiece tip.

The same hand cannot go from receiver-only to receiver-plus-pen without
moving the receiver. The sudden appearance of the silver-tipped pen pressed
against the handset, and the change from a tucked cord to a freely hanging
mouthpiece-plus-cord below the hand, proves the handset was turned and
re-gripped in the interval cut out between the side view and the closer
